name: Royal Orchid Hotels Ltd
title: Royal Orchid Hotels Ltd - 532699 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Royal Orchid FY26 consolidated revenue rose to INR384 crore and EBITDA to INR110 crore, but ICONIQA Mumbai's Ind AS hit cut PAT to INR33 crore; management gave no FY27 guidance.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations rose to INR384 crore from INR319 crore, with EBITDA of INR110 crore and PAT of INR33 crore after exceptional items (EPS INR11.74). Management said PAT growth excluding ICONIQA Mumbai was about 16.8%, with ICONIQA's first-year Ind AS hit of about INR15-16 crore (notional) and INR7.5 crore of pre-operating expense write-offs weighing on reported profit. Management said the West Asia conflict hit March cancellations and April-May ADR and occupancy, and declined to give FY27 or FY28 revenue and EBITDA guidance, saying it would revisit after Q1. A final dividend of INR2.5 per share was recommended.

financial_highlights.change: PAT growth excluding ICONIQA stated at about 16.8%

financial_highlights.value: About INR100 crore (INR88 crore consolidated plus about INR14 crore at associate)
About INR91 crore, including INR45 crore for ICONIQA Mumbai

financial_highlights.change: Q4 EBITDA about breakeven per analyst's reconciliation

financial_highlights.metric: Regenta Hotels Pvt Ltd (managed subsidiary) revenue
financial_highlights.change: vs about INR38-39 crore last year per analyst

financial_highlights.metric: Regenta Hotels Pvt Ltd EBITDA / PBT
financial_highlights.value: About INR20 crore EBITDA / about INR17 crore PBT after 5% brand fee

segments.name: ICONIQA Mumbai (about 290 keys, revenue share)
segments.commentary: Q4 occupancy about 62%, with January about 80%, February about 73%, and heavy March cancellations after the war began. April-May occupancy stated at about 81%. First-year Ind AS hit about INR15-16 crore (notional), plus INR7.5 crore of pre-operating expense write-offs.

segments.name: Managed hotels (Regenta Hotels Pvt Ltd)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR55-56 crore and EBITDA about INR20 crore for FY26, which an analyst said is roughly flat versus last year. Management did not give a FY27 segment outlook.

segments.name: Existing owned/leased hotels (ex-ICONIQA)
segments.commentary: EBITDA about INR103 crore. Managed hotels existing last year run at about 67-68% occupancy, and the blended managed occupancy of about 62% reflects new openings.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 or FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance; management will revisit after Q1 FY27.
Management says FY27 will be a better year than FY26 and that more hotels will be added in FY27 than in FY26.
ICONIQA Mumbai expected to be PAT-positive on a notional-Ind AS-excluded basis in FY27-28; PAT likely negative in FY27 due to Ind AS.
Vision 2030 targets 345 hotels and 22,000 keys, with Hampton by Hilton expected to be part of the roadmap.
Management declined to comment on whether cash PAT could reach INR100 crore by FY28.
capex_capacity: Portfolio of 52 signed hotels totalling about 3,600 keys; about 522 keys (around 500-plus) are revenue-share, with management hoping they open within FY27 but declining to give dates.
Around 7-8 hotels expected to open within the next 2-3 months, including Tirupati next week, Kota soon and a Hyderabad hotel shortly.
Five signed revenue-share hotels need only INR5-10 crore of capex each, to be funded internally.
Hampton by Hilton: 10-year agreement for about 125 hotels in 6 states (average about 75 keys), signings expected in FY27, with openings phased over the 10 years.
Maintenance and renovation capex is ongoing at existing hotels; a Bangalore resort added 28 wooden cottages, funded with a INR15 crore loan sanction plus internal surplus.
demand_pricing: FY26 ADR rose to about INR6,000+ from INR5,800, while occupancy was flat year on year; management said occupancy would have grown had the war not hit.
Q4 international guests about 19% (30,000 guests) versus 80.8% domestic.

Management cited the IndiGo disruption (about 15 days of lower occupancy across the group), Middle East carriers (about 40% of inbound India share) disrupted by the war, rising costs and labour codes, and tile supply delays from Morbi due to the LPG crisis.
Management said the last month post-war had hit ADR and occupancy and that costs were rising, including labour wages and fuel.

qa_highlights.question: Strategic levers for FY27 expansion, growth corridors and asset-light versus own-property balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 52 signed hotels (about 3,600 keys), a beefed-up development team, and inbound approaches from owners. The model is mostly managed, with some franchise and flexi-lease (revenue share with minimum guarantee).

qa_highlights.question: Debt and refinancing frameworks, given consolidated PAT of about INR25.11 crore for 9M FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said cash is about INR100 crore including the associate, bank borrowings about INR91 crore (including INR45 crore for ICONIQA), and the company could become debt-free at once. Funds are earmarked for flexi-lease capex.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the West Asia crisis on Q4 and ICONIQA, and medium-term FY27-28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given because of geopolitical uncertainty. Management said the last month post-war had hurt ADR and occupancy, and it will revisit after Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why take small managed hotels (e.g. a 70-key Hyderabad hotel) and what is the managed-segment profit outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Keshav Baljee said there are per-hotel minimum monthly fee thresholds, rising yearly. Portfolio brands are Regenta (60-80+ keys), Regenta Place (40-80) and Z by Regenta (about 50 keys, franchise). Chairman said scale matters, with about 100 hotels at INR3-5 lakh per month each.

qa_highlights.question: When will cash PAT inflect, and could it reach INR100 crore by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited cash growth and said FY26 PAT was hit by ICONIQA's notional Ind AS charge. Chairman declined to give forward-looking statements on cash PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ICONIQA's EBITDA swing small after INR7 crore of top-line growth, and when does it become PAT-profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said launch and marketing costs (classified as operating expense) drove the weak EBITDA. Management expects PAT positive in FY27-28 excluding notional Ind AS, but PAT likely negative in FY27 including it.

risks_watch: Auditor disagreement led to INR5.5 crore of pre-operating expenses (plus INR2 crore earlier) being written off; management said all write-offs are now taken.
Revenue-share ramp-up (about 522 keys) depends on owner construction, which is affected by cost increases, Morbi tile shortages and LPG disruption; no opening dates given.
Ind AS notional charge on ICONIQA will weigh on PAT in FY27.
Managed-segment earnings flat in FY26; minimum-fee and portfolio restructuring is planned.
Management flagged proposed minimum-wage increases and the new labour code as cost risks.
Hampton by Hilton ramp-up and key count not quantified; first signings expected in FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term platform and pipeline but notably cautious on near-term numbers: management refused to give FY27 or FY28 guidance, citing the West Asia war, cost inflation and fluid conditions. Several answers were evasive on timelines (openings, revenue-share keys, cash PAT).
key_quotes: We don't want to give you something that we will then walk back next quarter.
I don't think we should give any statements like this. At this stage, because of this uncertainty in the world, I will refrain from giving any forward-looking statements.
We can become debt free even today also in one shot but there is a plan that we will grow the company
Execution is becoming our biggest differentiator.

growth.why: No numerical FY27/FY28 revenue or EBITDA guidance was given, management only said FY27 will be better than FY26 with more hotel additions, backed by 7-8 openings in 2-3 months and a 52-hotel signed pipeline (~3,600 keys) without dates, while the West Asia conflict hit March and April-May demand.
